title: Cryogenics
description: Near absolute zero, matter forgets it is many particles. Superfluids and Bose-Einstein condensates.

puzzle.goal: Identical particles with integer spin may pile any number into the same quantum state. In a gas held at temperature T with chemical potential μ, find the mean number of particles occupying a single state of energy ε.
puzzle.name: Bose–Einstein distribution (condensation temperature)
puzzle.ask: Summing the occupation over all momentum states at μ = 0 gives a maximum density ζ(3/2)/λ_T³ with ζ(3/2) = 2.612 and λ_T = √(2πħ²/(m kB T)); below that temperature the excess condenses. Find the condensation temperature Tc = (2πħ²/(m kB))·(N/2.612)^(2/3) for helium-4 at the density of the liquid.

vars.n: mean occupation number of the state

puzzle.method: Maximise the number of ways to distribute particles among states at fixed total energy and number (or sum the geometric series Σ e^(−n(ε−μ)/kBT) over occupation n in the grand canonical ensemble).
